result.title: Pixel Auto-Encoder: Reconstructing Language Model Activations Through Pixel Art
result.summary: Interpreting the high-dimensional internal representations of large language models (LLMs) remains a challenging problem. Recent approaches have explored translating these representations into human-understandable forms, particularly natural language. In this work, we explore the use of images as an alternative target modality for interpreting LLM activations. As a first step toward this goal, we introduce Pixel Auto-Encoder, which converts intermediate LLM activations into $32 \times 32$, 32-color pixel art and reconstructs them for subsequent computation within the model. By encouraging the intermediate representations to resemble predefined concept images, we investigate whether LLM activations can be expressed visually while preserving the model's language capabilities. We find that the model can produce target-aligned images for some concepts, and that replacing pixel representations with concept images can influence next-token predictions. However, we also observe a trade-off between visual alignment and language-model performance, as well as sensitivity to pixel-level changes that are difficult to interpret visually. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and limitations of image-based representations of LLM activations.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 Pixel Auto-Encoder，把纯文本 LLM 的中间激活编码为 32×32、32 色的像素画，并在模型内部再重建回激活，考察激活能否被表示为可供人观看的图像、且是否保持语言能力。
